about.title: Pico Rivera Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a crash on a Pico Rivera roadway takes someone's life, the family left behind faces grief alongside confusing legal questions. Los Angeles County recorded traffic deaths on local streets in recent years, and while every death is different, California law gives certain surviving family members — spouses, domestic partners, and children first, followed by other dependents or heirs — the right to pursue a wrongful death claim. This is a civil action, entirely separate from any criminal charges that may or may not follow a fatal collision. Families in Pico Rivera often have questions about funeral costs, lost income the deceased would have provided, and the loss of companionship and guidance that can't be replaced. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney in our network who can walk through your specific situation, explain the two-year filing deadline, and help you understand whether a claim makes sense for your family.

whyChoose.title: What Pico Rivera Families Should Know

items.title: Limited Standing, Clear Priority
items.desc: California law restricts who may file a wrongful death claim, generally giving priority to a spouse, domestic partner, or children before other dependents or heirs. An attorney can clarify where your family fits.

items.title: The Two-Year Clock is Real
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims involving a government entity often carry a much shorter deadline. Missing it can end a family's ability to recover anything.

items.title: Civil Case, Separate Path
items.desc: A wrongful death claim proceeds independently of any criminal case connected to the collision, meaning families aren't required to wait on a criminal outcome to pursue their own claim.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: California generally gives first priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing. An attorney can review your family's circumstances to determine who qualifies.

items.question: Is there something specific about Pico Rivera roads I should mention to an attorney?
items.answer: Yes — corridors like Rosemead Boulevard, Whittier Boulevard, Slauson Avenue, and Paramount Boulevard see the most reported collisions locally, and crash reports here tend to cluster on Thursday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. Sharing where and when the crash happened helps an attorney understand the available public records.

items.question: How long do we have to file a claim?
items.answer: Generally two years from the date of death under California law, though claims against a government entity — such as a city or county — often require a formal notice within a much shorter window, sometimes just months. It's worth speaking to an attorney promptly to avoid missing a deadline.
